correctness.rationale: For c>0, d>=1 and usual geodesic angular distance, positive definite iff d<=3 or c>=pi, with strict PD in the positive cases. C_n^(3/2)=P_(n+1)' and the derivative recurrence reduce the S4 Schoenberg integral to (n+1)(n+2)/(2n+3) times J_n-J_(n+2). Mehler--Dirichlet gives an Abel cosine transform. Its cutoff s^(5/2) term gives n^(-7/2) for each J; adjacent-frequency subtraction gives the claimed n^(-5/2) oscillatory coefficient, while the t^2 log t origin term cancels to n^(-3) after the prefactor. Beta(1/2,3)=16/15 and Gamma(7/2)=15 sqrt(pi)/8 fix the amplitude; geometric Cesaro means of cos and cos^2 force infinitely many negative coefficients. For c>=pi, arcsin(cos(theta)) has positive odd monomial coefficients and Schur positivity of the square gives strictly positive power coefficients; for d<=3 the cited Gneiting theorem gives the low-dimensional claim. A new independent checker verified 36 exact Legendre recurrences and sign changes in three finite cutoff samples. Numeric samples are not the infinite sign proof. Pointwise O_c error not uniform near c=0 or pi.
